description: A highly destructive caterpillar pest found in tropical and subtropical regions. The larvae feed on leaves, flowers, and fruits of many crops, especially tomato and cotton, causing major yield losses.
symptoms: Small holes on young leaves caused by early larvae feeding
Small entry holes on fruits, often near the stalk
Damaged or mined fruits with internal feeding
Fruits stop growing, ripen early, and drop from the plant
Damaged flowers and pierced seed pods in legumes
spread: Adult moths laying eggs on leaves and fruits
Migration of adult moths between crop fields
management: Regular monitoring of crops for eggs and young larvae
Use pheromone traps to monitor moth populations
Use resistant or tolerant crop varieties when available
biological_control: Release of parasitoid wasps such as Trichogramma species
Predators such as lady beetles, lacewings, and birds
prevention: Field sanitation and removal of crop residues
Use pheromone traps for early detection
Maintain balanced fertilization to avoid excessive plant growth
